meta.purpose: Evidence gaps and safe working interpretations; no manual response is required to publish.

state_legend.answered: The specific observation is supported, not every future travel condition.
state_legend.open: Evidence remains missing; no unsupported value is substituted.
state_legend.interpreted: Working interpretation of the trip brief, not a new fact from an external source.

questions.question: Which hotels have the most MICHELIN listings within 60 minutes by bus?
questions.answer: No verified bus-only ranking has been established. The old zone model estimated 24/24 for every hotel using assumptions and additional modes; neither that count nor its 20-minute tiebreaker proves a real journey.
questions.problem: Official fares or a route map do not establish door-to-door travel time. Walks, waits, transfers, service date and the return after dinner are missing.
questions.substitution: No unsupported number is substituted. The public field stays blank where official evidence is missing.
questions.how_to_close: Capture dated RTC itineraries from each named hotel to each listing, including access walks, waits, transfers and return service. Count only documented journeys meeting the threshold; do not use Monorail or Loop as bus substitutes.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.question: Rank hotels by how many Michelin restaurants are within 1 hour by subway or bus.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.answer: Las Vegas has no subway or metro. Buses (RTC Deuce/SDX), the Monorail and the Vegas Loop were substituted, and separate fares were checked for each.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.problem: Because the Strip is ~4 miles long and Chinatown ~3 miles west of it, all 24 Michelin listings sit inside 60 minutes of every hotel in the dataset. The literal metric gives a flat 24/24 to all of them and ranks nothing.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.substitution: A second column — Michelin restaurants within a 20-minute one-way trip — is shown alongside the 60-minute figure and is used as the ranking tiebreaker.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.how_to_close: Nothing to close. It is a property of the city. If a stricter or looser threshold is preferred, the zone matrix in data/transit.json allows recomputation in one step.

questions.question: How is a 1–2-week trip reconciled with the preferred 15–18 February span?
questions.answer: 15–18 February 2027 is three nights. The autonomous working basis is 15–22 February (seven nights, preferred arrival retained). A possible 14-night option is 15 February–1 March, within the allowed period.
questions.problem: The full preferred three-night span cannot contain a seven-night trip. Seven- and 14-night prices have not been obtained as final official totals; neither may be scaled into the other.
questions.substitution: No unsupported number is substituted. The public field stays blank where official evidence is missing.
questions.how_to_close: Continue all comparable hotel quote research on the stated seven-night basis. Keep the 14-night option separately unpriced until a full official quote is available; do not require manual input just to publish.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.question: Trip length is 1–2 weeks, but the preferred window is 2027-02-15 → 2027-02-18.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.answer: 2027-02-15 → 2027-02-18 is three nights. Pricing therefore uses the 7-night block starting on the preferred arrival date (2027-02-15 → 2027-02-22), which satisfies the stated 7-night basis and still starts on the requested date.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.problem: If the couple literally wants a 3-night trip, the 7-night totals on this site are about 2.3× too large, and the extra nights are pure cost.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.substitution: 7-night totals are presented because that is the stated basis. A 14-night variant is NOT priced — see F-17.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.how_to_close: Ask the couple which they meant. If 3 nights, re-run the price capture with checkout 2027-02-18; every slug and window in data/hotels.json is ready for it.

questions.question: Which 2026 MICHELIN listings are starred rather than Bib Gourmand or Recommended?
questions.answer: Four Las Vegas restaurants are starred: Joël Robuchon (2 stars); L’Atelier, Guy Savoy and é (1 each). China Poblano, Esther’s Kitchen and YEN Viet are Bib Gourmand; 17 others are Recommended. The complete Las Vegas subset was checked against the official tables.
questions.problem: Historic video captions and stars awarded to another branch/city are not evidence for a current Las Vegas star. Two official press pages have differing publication dates; the exact announcement date is not inferred.
questions.substitution: No unsupported number is substituted. The public field stays blank where official evidence is missing.
questions.how_to_close: Status is supported for the 2026 selection. Recheck the official Guide if a later selection is published before travel.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.question: Which of the 24 Michelin restaurants are starred, and which are only listed?
previous_pass_2026_11_27.answer: Four are starred: Joël Robuchon (2★), L'Atelier Robuchon (1★), Guy Savoy (1★), é by José Andrés (1★). The other 20 listings carry no star: 3 are Bib Gourmand (China Poblano, Esther's Kitchen, Yen Viet Kitchen) and 17 are Recommended.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.problem: There are no three-star restaurants in Las Vegas, and no guide existed at all between 2010 and 2025 — so most online 'Michelin star' claims for Vegas are stale.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.substitution: Each restaurant row on the site shows the award class separately from the name, so nothing reads as 'starred' by accident.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.how_to_close: Closed. Cross-checked against the Michelin press release, LVCVA and Las Vegas Weekly.

questions.question: What can be stated about dinner for two without inventing a complete bill?
questions.answer: Official fixed-menu/set food subtotals for two are supported for Partage, Anima by EDO, Stubborn Seed, Wing Lei, China Poblano, Kabuto, SoulBelly BBQ, COTE, Sparrow + Wolf, Mott 32 weekday lunch and Estiatorio Milos daily lunch. Michael Mina’s $590 printed subtotal is supported separately but the venue is currently temporarily closed. Guy Savoy’s dishes do not establish a meal. KAME’s own contact page now prints $350/$500 menu offerings, but the extracted amounts do not explicitly state a per-person unit, so its two-adult subtotal stays blank; the menu observation is shown separately (FV-08).
questions.problem: Final tax, service/gratuity, drinks, supplements and trip-date menu/availability are unverified. A menu subtotal is not an all-in bill.
questions.substitution: No unsupported number is substituted. The public field stays blank where official evidence is missing.
questions.how_to_close: Use operator-linked menus and read-only official reservation details for the exact date. Record the full two-person bill basis and any mandatory charges; never place dummy bookings, deposits or payment authorizations to discover a price.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.question: What does dinner for two cost at each Michelin restaurant?
previous_pass_2026_11_27.answer: Four venues print a real number on their official pages: Michael Mina ($295++ per person), Anima by EDO ($85 per person), KAME Omakase ($500 per person, from its own OpenTable description), and Guy Savoy (official à la carte dishes $100–$290 → $200–$580 for two; Krug Chef's Table 10-course $1,500/pp → $3,000 for two, per the Caesars menu effective 11.5.2026). All figures are before tax, gratuity and wine. Everything else leaves the cell blank. Note Michael Mina is currently marked Temporarily closed — see Q-11.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.problem: Las Vegas fine-dining rooms publish menus without prices, and the ones that do publish (tasting menus) change them seasonally. Inventing a range would violate the no-inference rule; the Guy Savoy cell shows only arithmetic on printed official prices.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.substitution: Blank cells plus a 'price on request' marker rather than an estimate.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.how_to_close: Book a table on OpenTable for a dummy date and read the deposit or prepay amount, or phone the numbers listed in data/restaurants.json. 17 of the 24 venues now publish a phone number and can be called in one sitting.

questions.question: Is a private/in-room bathroom and queen-or-larger bed proved for each hotel offer?
questions.answer: Named-room descriptions were read for 11 candidates: Caesars Palace, Venetian, Palazzo, Wynn, Desert Rose, Cliffs at Peace Canyon, Hilton at Resorts World, Crockfords, Bellagio, Cosmopolitan and MGM Grand. Specific King/Queen beds and described in-room bathroom facilities are supported only for the named variants. A room description is not a trip-date allocation, exclusive-use guarantee or qualified offer. All 34 candidates retain explicit nulls for missing evidence.
questions.problem: A property homepage, a building-level reference or an assigned-on-arrival rate cannot guarantee a specific bed, private room or bathroom for the offered rate.
questions.substitution: No unsupported number is substituted. The public field stays blank where official evidence is missing.
questions.how_to_close: Obtain a named-room official rate block for two adults and the exact dates, with bed/bath terms. Confirm the quoted inventory is the hotel’s own offer rather than an independently managed unit.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.question: Does each hotel room actually have a private bathroom and a queen-or-larger bed?
previous_pass_2026_11_27.answer: Most do — every four- and five-star property in the dataset states a private bathroom and a king or queen bed in its rate block. Three exceptions are flagged: rooms sold as 'assigned on arrival' (LINQ, Flamingo, SAHARA, Golden Nugget) do not guarantee the bed type, and Bluegreen Club 36's private bathroom is not stated.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.problem: A promotional rate on an unassigned room is the cheapest thing on the site but does not meet the couple's bed requirement until check-in.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.substitution: Assigned-on-arrival rates are shown but flagged, never ranked as the default pick.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.how_to_close: Book a NAMED room class, not 'Run of House' / 'Room Type Assigned on Arrival'. On Booking.com that means opening the room-type list and picking a specific king or queen category.

questions.question: Which stay week and future purchase date are actually cheapest?
questions.answer: No cheapest week or purchase day is established. There are 30 possible seven-night start dates from 15 February through 16 March, with checkout by 23 March. The old four-window OTA sample was not exhaustive or like-for-like. Wynn’s published Cyber booking window is 20 November–4 December 2026, not proof of the lowest future price.
questions.problem: Comparable official final totals, room/rate terms and enough stay windows are missing. Future prices cannot be guaranteed from one promotion or snapshot.
questions.substitution: No unsupported number is substituted. The public field stays blank where official evidence is missing.
questions.how_to_close: Compare exact official seven-night totals for the same eligible named room, fee/tax basis, occupancy, currency and cancellation terms. Keep capture timestamps and sale conditions; do not claim market-wide cheapest from a partial sample.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.question: Which week inside 2027-02-15 → 2027-03-23 is actually cheapest?
previous_pass_2026_11_27.answer: No market-wide cheapest week is established. Booking.com snapshots show lower 8–15 March quotes for some measured large resorts; a separate sample of official property booking engines found 15–22 February cheapest at the properties checked. These snapshots differ in property coverage, room/rate terms, taxes and resort-fee treatment, and the Venetian direct result has an unclear 4+ guest-suite label. The Venetian figure from 25 Nov ($2,407 for 8–15 Mar vs $3,757 for 15–22 Feb) was withdrawn on 26 Nov: Booking.com's own Venetian page showed US$5,185.05 (15–22 Feb) and €4,472.36 (8–15 Mar), both including taxes and fees (F-39). The Palazzo and Cosmopolitan 25 Nov figures have not been re-checked (F-44).
previous_pass_2026_11_27.problem: The dated samples are not like-for-like and will change before the trip. A 26 Nov re-fetch showed changed official-engine rates within one day, and the Venetian direct result had a confusing 4+ guest label. The current evidence cannot show that one window is cheapest across all eligible hotels; see F-30.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.substitution: The site reports the Booking.com quote comparisons as third-party snapshots and flags the conflicting official-engine sample; it does not recommend moving away from the preferred dates based on these alone.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.how_to_close: Compare the exact 7-night dates, same named room, resort fee, taxes and cancellation terms directly on each hotel's official booking engine. Recheck close to purchase; no specific booking date is endorsed from this mixed-source snapshot.

questions.question: Which social links are verified from official venue cross-links?
questions.answer: Twenty restaurant Instagram profiles are approved from official-site cross-links or opened venue/brand profiles with recorded identity evidence. L’Atelier’s dormant profile exposed tags but no clear operator-domain/control evidence, so it remains unapproved; the research link is preserved. Shared brands, dormant feeds and The LINQ parent account/channel are labelled. Neon’s TikTok is an official-site cross-link, not a successfully opened target. Historical venue/creator videos and the parallel oEmbed check are preserved with attribution on Flagged for Review, not used as award, hour or price evidence.
questions.problem: A guessed handle, venue-like tags, a look-alike account or a creator title cannot establish operator control or current factual accuracy. The 2026 Guide—not a stale bio or another city’s branch—determines the award. Some targets show mixed error/content responses or automated-access limits.
questions.substitution: No unsupported number is substituted. The public field stays blank where official evidence is missing.
questions.how_to_close: For each remaining gap, establish operator control through an official cross-link, matching official domain/location or other explicit primary identity evidence, then record target response and platform scope. Preserve unconfirmed discoveries as attributed research; do not fill a blank from a plausible username.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.question: What are each restaurant's YouTube, TikTok and Instagram links?
previous_pass_2026_11_27.answer: YouTube is recorded for every one of the 24 restaurants (69 links), and those video links were not opened, so whether each still plays is unverified. Instagram is now filled for 19 of the 24 restaurants and TikTok for 2 (Lamaii, Esther's Kitchen); for the five activities Instagram is filled for 4 of 5 and TikTok for 3 of 5. Those coverage counts come from the 2026-11-27 social sweep recorded in F-53, not from this session's own page visits.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.problem: Handles are not printed on most official pages, so a handle found nowhere but a search result is weak evidence: a wrong handle creates a dead or, worse, someone else's account. Creator videos that tag a venue are not the venue's account.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.substitution: Blank rather than guessed, and every filled activity cell now states where the handle came from (activities page, 'Where each social link came from'). The Neon Museum is the strongest case: it prints both its Instagram and TikTok in its own site navigation.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.how_to_close: Open each remaining restaurant's official page footer or its OpenTable profile and look for the venue's own link. 5 Instagram gaps and 22 TikTok gaps remain; TikTok is the hardest because many venues never created one. Anything not printed by the venue or its booking profile should stay blank (F-53).

questions.question: Are published hours and exceptions confirmed for February–March 2027?
questions.answer: The field log records current official hours read on 27 November 2026. Neon has a specific 2027 Admission page. Current weekly hours are not a guarantee of trip-date operation.
questions.problem: The trip begins less than three months after this audit, not 15 months. Holiday/seasonal notices can be date-specific. High Roller’s own opening/ticket blocks conflict; its complete weekly hours remain blank.
questions.substitution: No unsupported number is substituted. The public field stays blank where official evidence is missing.
questions.how_to_close: Re-fetch the official schedule and reservation calendar for each chosen date, distinguish dated exceptions from weekly service, and recheck shortly before travel. Do not reuse 2026 Thanksgiving/December closures as 2027 weekly rules.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.question: Are the opening hours current for the trip dates (February–March 2027)?
previous_pass_2026_11_27.answer: Hours were captured on 2026-11-25 and are the venues' current published hours. Several are seasonal or reduced: Wing Lei and L'Atelier are closed two weekdays, SoulBelly closes Mondays, Michael Mina publishes block closures.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.problem: A February 2027 trip is roughly 3 months from the November 2026 capture date, and Las Vegas restaurants frequently adjust seasonal or holiday schedules.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.substitution: The 'exceptions' column records every closure noticed, and every row links to the official page so hours can be re-checked in one click.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.how_to_close: Re-check the four starred restaurants and Michael Mina two weeks before travel — these are the ones that will ruin an evening if they are dark.

questions.question: Do official hotel totals include every mandatory fee and tax?
questions.answer: No fully qualified final seven-night offer was established. Caesars shows an error banner plus tax-exclusive nightly amounts; Wynn shows tax-exclusive nightly averages; Venetian rendered no quote. Hilton Resorts World’s exact-date engine prints a fully itemized $2,200.15 total for 15–22 February, two adults, Deluxe One King, including listed room tax/resort fee/fee tax. That observation is reproduced separately, not promoted to a qualifying offer: promotion eligibility, deposit/cancellation and private-use guarantee remain unverified.
questions.problem: Rounded averages and changing fee/tax bases cannot be promoted into exact final totals. The previous generic resort-fee/tax uplift was not a valid hotel-specific quote.
questions.substitution: No unsupported number is substituted. The public field stays blank where official evidence is missing.
questions.how_to_close: Read an itemized final stay total from an official quote without submitting a reservation. Record mandatory fees, tax, deposit and cancellation terms. Do not add a blanket tax rate or multiply rounded averages into an exact offer.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.question: Do the hotel prices include resort fees and tax?
previous_pass_2026_11_27.answer: Not consistently. Booking.com search totals generally exclude the resort fee and local tax; the Wynn property pages quote room plus $55/night resort fee but exclude 13.38% tax.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.problem: This is why Wynn shows $4,378 in one place and $5,828 in another for the same week. Comparing the two bases directly understates the Wynn group by roughly a third.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.substitution: Both figures are published side by side with the basis stated in the row, rather than picking one and hiding the other.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.how_to_close: Add the resort fee (typically $35–$55/night on the Strip) and 13.38% tax to every Booking.com total before comparing. That is roughly +$250 to +$390 per week on a mid-Strip room.

questions.question: Do holidays, conventions or races change the chosen week’s price or service?
questions.answer: No causal event-price relationship or complete February/March 2027 convention/transport calendar has been established in this integration.
questions.problem: A holiday or event listing alone cannot establish higher hotel prices, closed restaurants or altered bus service. Earlier causal language and incomplete event checks are not a verified answer.
questions.substitution: No unsupported number is substituted. The public field stays blank where official evidence is missing.
questions.how_to_close: Read official LVCVA/event-organizer calendars and RTC service alerts for the exact stay. Compare official hotel totals before asserting that an event changes price; leave the effect unverified if it cannot be separated from room/rate changes.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.question: Is there a convention, race or holiday in the chosen week that changes the price?
previous_pass_2026_11_27.answer: The Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix is NOT in this window — the 2027 race is 18–20 November 2027, well outside 15 Feb–23 Mar. US Presidents' Day falls on 15 Feb 2027, the first day of the preferred window.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.problem: Presidents' Day is a long weekend and the February week is the most expensive of the four measured. The calendar fact is verified; the causal link to the price is not, so it is labelled a likely driver, not a proven one.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.substitution: Nothing changed — both facts are stated with that distinction.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.how_to_close: Check the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority events calendar and the Las Vegas Motor Speedway schedule for the chosen week. NASCAR's spring race weekend is traditionally in early March.

questions.question: Is Michael Mina, or any other listing, confirmed open during this 2027 trip?
questions.answer: Michael Mina’s current Bellagio page is labelled temporarily closed and its hours block says Monday–Sunday: Closed. The printed tasting-menu price remains visible. That proves the present warning, not that it will still be closed or reopened in February 2027.
questions.problem: No trip-date reopening confirmation was obtained. A printed menu on a dormant venue is not a bookable dinner.
questions.substitution: No unsupported number is substituted. The public field stays blank where official evidence is missing.
questions.how_to_close: Recheck the official page and exact-date reservation calendar. Exclude the venue from any committed dinner schedule until operating dates and availability are confirmed.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.question: Is every MICHELIN-listed restaurant in the dataset actually open for a February 2027 trip?
previous_pass_2026_11_27.answer: One is not. Michael Mina at Bellagio publishes "Monday to Sunday: Closed" in its Hours of operation block and carries a "Temporarily closed" label on its own Bellagio page. Its $590++ tasting-menu price is still printed on that page, so a reader could easily mistake a dormant venue for an available one.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.problem: A price on a closed restaurant is worse than a blank: it looks bookable. Grouping this row with live venues would put a phantom dinner into a 7-night plan.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.how_to_close: Restaurant row kept, but with the closure stated on the row and flagged **F-23**. No reopen date is published, so no date is assumed.

questions.question: Which restaurant/activity details changed in this fresh official-source sweep?
questions.answer: Corrections include China Poblano Sunday closing at 10 PM; Wing Lei’s open-day list including Friday/Saturday; Milos Friday/Saturday closing at 11 PM; Mob Museum recurring daily 9 AM–9 PM; Fremont Music Reels starting 6 PM; Neon’s 2027 ticket regime; and Kabuto’s printed phone 702-676-1044. Guy Savoy’s complete price was withdrawn. Completed T23 discoveries were independently reopened here: Yen Viet Kitchen’s operator-linked storefront prints Mon, Wed–Sun 10 AM–8:30 PM (Tue closed); KAME has explicit seatings/phone/cancellation rules on /contact-us/; four more fixed-menu/lunch subtotals are supported; four more hotels have named room descriptions; Neon’s early/late-arrival price rule starts January 1, 2027.
questions.problem: Some fields remain unknown: a full Guy Savoy weekly schedule was not exposed, Sparrow + Wolf and other independent pages did not yield complete hours, and High Roller has contradictory blocks.
questions.substitution: No unsupported number is substituted. The public field stays blank where official evidence is missing.
questions.how_to_close: Corrections are complete for these observed fields. The verification page lists every remaining null and its source reference; never mark an entire row verified merely because one field was confirmed.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.question: Do the published opening hours in this dataset survive a second check against the venues' own sites?
previous_pass_2026_11_27.answer: Five rows needed correction: Joël Robuchon (hours blank → Tue–Sat 5:00–9:30 PM), Partage (blank → Tue–Sat 5–9 PM, published on the Contact page only), Sparrow + Wolf (no hours published at all), KAME Omakase (no weekly hours on its booking page) and Michael Mina (closed). Nineteen of 24 rows now carry a verified hours string.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.problem: Two of the five were blank because the hours live on a secondary page — Partage on /contact, Robuchon in an "Hours of operation" detail block rather than the header. A single-page check misses both.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.how_to_close: All five corrected or explicitly left blank with the reason recorded. See FLAGS.md **F-22 to F-25**.

questions.question: Were all official hotel links and all external/social links checked live?
questions.answer: No exhaustive live check is claimed for every external/media link. The parallel T20 record attempted all original 32 hotel reference URLs (21 live, 10 refused, 1 sibling). This pass independently read the specific source pages in the live field manifest, including Hilton’s engine/room and T23’s new Crockfords, Bellagio, Cosmopolitan and MGM King pages. That adds room-specific evidence, not a repeat live-check guarantee for all hotel references, a final offer or bus route.
questions.problem: A structurally valid href is not a successful remote fetch or field verification. A refusal by automated access is not necessarily a broken browser link.
questions.substitution: No unsupported number is substituted. The public field stays blank where official evidence is missing.
questions.how_to_close: Re-open each unchecked reference and record the response/redirect target, property identity and field evidence. Keep blocked/unavailable distinct. Do not claim zero broken external links from the local HTML validator.

previous_pass_2026_11_27.question: Are the hotels' own websites still live at the URLs this site links to?
previous_pass_2026_11_27.answer: Closed as far as this environment allows (finished 2026-11-27). All 32 hotel official URLs have now been checked: 21 of 32 are confirmed live by fetch (including Green Valley Ranch and Red Rock verified 2026-11-27), 10 refuse automated access (Wynn, Encore, Vdara, Secret Suites, NoMad, W, Bluegreen Club 36, Waldorf Astoria, The Signature at MGM Grand, and Crockfords which returned HTTP 500), 1 (Nobu at Caesars) opens but lands on the parent property's page, and 0 remain unopened (F-49).
previous_pass_2026_11_27.problem: Hotel brand sites move constantly — MGM, Caesars, Marriott and Hilton have all reorganised property URLs. Linking a moved page is a small failure, but claiming it was verified when it was not is the failure the brief actually cares about.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.substitution: Every card also shows the Booking.com link the price came from. Where that link is a dated search-results list rather than a property page (15 rows), the card says 'Price source — dated search list, not a room quote' (F-48), because the link proves the search, not the room.
previous_pass_2026_11_27.how_to_close: The 10 refused rows can only be closed from a normal browser or by calling the property — this environment is blocked by their CDNs. That is an access limit, not a data gap; the label says so.

questions.question: What personal preferences remain unknown without blocking publication?
questions.answer: No total/ nightly hotel budget, number of tasting-menu dinners, dietary/allergy needs, walking limits, accessibility requirements or refundable-versus-prepaid preference was supplied in the available brief. No preference is invented. The dashboard and evidence register are usable without an immediate response.
questions.problem: A cheapest-looking room or restrictive menu may be unsuitable once those constraints are known; no purchase or personalized best-fit claim is justified yet.
questions.substitution: Keep options and clear evidence gaps rather than silently choose a price ceiling, diet, walking allowance or non-refundable rate.
questions.how_to_close: Record these constraints before any actual booking or final personalized ranking. Continue source verification and publication autonomously in the meantime; no form or manual approval is required for this release.
